decision_conditions:
Reason : 1 - There are no public benefits that would outweigh the harm caused by this proposed advert. The proposed advert by reason of its excessive scale, illumination and prominent positioning would represent an overly dominant and visually intrusive feature. It would harm the character and appearance of the adjacent conservation area and would adversely affect the setting of nearby listed buildings failing to meet policies LP1 and LP3.  

The proposed advert would result in an unacceptable increase in the level of street clutter and would have an unacceptable impact on amenity in terms of light pollution failing to meet policies LP1, LP2, LP9 and LP14.

The application currently fails to demonstrate that adverse ecological effects of an advert of this scale would be avoided or appropriately mitigated and requires further information to be considered, failing to meet policy LP55.

The proposed advert would fail to improve the character and appearance of the town centre failing to meet policy WT20. 

The proposed advert due to its scale and location would harm public safety in that the advert would be considered a distraction to drivers, would hinder visibility of the nearby junction and would restrict the width of the pavement with misleading information provided to illustrate a greater width of pavement failing to meet the requirements of policy LP50.

The proposed development therefore conflicts with Policies WT20, LP1, LP2, LP3, LP9, LP14 and LP50 of the Wandsworth Local Plan (2023).

Reason : 2 - The proposed advert would result in an unacceptable increase in the level of street clutter and would have an unacceptable impact on visual amenity of the town centre and general light levels failing to meet policies LP1, LP2, LP9 and LP14.

Reason : 3 - The application currently fails to demonstrate that adverse ecological effects of an advert of this scale would be avoided or appropriately mitigated and requires further information to be considered, failing to meet policy LP55.
Reason : 4 - The proposed advert would fail to improve the character and appearance of the town centre failing to meet policy WT20.

Reason : 5 - The proposed advert due to its scale and location would harm public safety in that the advert would be considered a distraction to drivers, would hinder visibility of the nearby junction and would restrict the width of the pavement with misleading information provided to illustrate a greater width of pavement failing to meet the requirements of policy LP50.
site_name: Advertising Hoarding On Pavement Junction Of Wandsworth High Street And Buckhold Road
description: Erection of a freestanding digital portrait-format LED advertising display (6m x 4m), located on land to the front of Southside Shopping Centre.
